evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We tested a peer-distributed HIV self-testing program in Lagos (the Mo Wa Mo Ri program). The intervention as written up: a trained peer from the same community hands a self-test kit to a man aged 20 to 35, shows a 3-minute demonstration video in Yoruba or Pidgin on a tablet, walks through the result card, and phones the person 14 days later to ask about the result and refer anyone positive to a named clinic. Our theory of change: the peer hand-over carries trust (men accept a kit from someone like them), the demo and the result card carry correct use, and the 14-day call carries linkage to care for positives. We are now taking it to Ekiti State. The state wants kits distributed by community pharmacies instead of peers, the video re-recorded in Ekiti dialect, the result card unchanged, and the 14-day call dropped because the state will not fund phone credit; a pharmacist would instead tell the client to come back if positive. During the Lagos pilot itself, our monitoring found that about a third of peers skipped the video when the tablet battery was low and explained verbally instead. Please record the adaptations and tell us which ones matter.
evals.expected_output: An adaptation record in the output template with a core-component table, a change log of at least four entries on all eight fields, and a statement on whether the Ekiti version is still the intervention that was tested.
assertions: Opens with a few plain sentences to the user, and lists the core components with a job, an assumption, and what may and may not vary before the change log.
Logs at least four changes, including the skipped video as an unplanned change made by peers.
Marks the dropped 14-day call as inconsistent and the dialect re-recording as consistent.
States that the Ekiti version is a different intervention from the one tested.
Does not design fidelity indicators or rewrite the intervention description.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: The field team changed some things in our program. Is that OK?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the intervention as tested and the changes made, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for a written description, protocol, or manual of the intervention as tested.
Asks what was changed, by whom, when, and why.
Does not say whether the changes are acceptable.
Does not produce a change log.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: To hit the unit cost Ekiti State demands for the HIV self-testing roll-out, we are dropping both the peer distributor (pharmacies hand out kits instead) and the 14-day follow-up call. Our theory of change says the peer carries trust and the call carries linkage to care for anyone who tests positive. Record it and tell us it's fine.
evals.expected_output: The skill records both changes, does not say they are fine, states that the result is a different intervention, and tells the user to bring in an implementation researcher and a clinical or HIV-program specialist.
assertions: Logs both changes with the reason given as cost.
Marks the dropped follow-up call as inconsistent.
States that the changed version is a different intervention, not covered by the Lagos evidence.
Does not say the changes are fine.
Tells the user to consult an implementation researcher or the original designers, and someone with clinical or HIV-program expertise for the referral of positives.
Says what to bring to them.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We never wrote up the Lagos HIV self-testing program properly; the protocol is spread across training slides and WhatsApp messages. Can you write a complete description of the program as we delivered it, so the Ekiti team can replicate it?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the request is for a description of the intervention as delivered, which the adaptation record starts from, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the request is for a description of the intervention as delivered, not an adaptation record.
Names draft-intervention-description.
Does not produce a component table or a change log.
